clue.text: Made no progress in the fog on waters at sea

indicators.note: being at sea means confused and lost, so the letters before it are thrown into disorder

parts.note: all fourteen letters of these three words are the fodder

explanation.surface: A boat stuck in fog out on the water, going nowhere.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes effort that yields no advance at all, which is exactly failing to make progress.

clue.text: Brutes escaping from dog rescue

indicators.note: the answer slips out of the run of letters across the next two words

parts.note: found running across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: Vicious dogs breaking out of an animal rescue centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Ogres are monstrous, cruel giants of folklore, so the word serves for any brutish people.

clue.text: Lie envious uncle spread in French cooking school

indicators.note: spread suggests the letters scattered about and laid out in a different arrangement

parts.note: all fifteen letters of these three words are the fodder

explanation.surface: A jealous uncle spreading falsehoods about a cookery school.
explanation.definitionFit: Nouvelle cuisine is the light, artfully presented style of cookery that emerged in France in the 1970s.

clue.text: After onset of winter, warm cereal's required

indicators.note: the onset of something is its beginning, so only the first letter is taken

parts.note: the opening letter of winter
to warm something is to heat it

explanation.surface: Hot cereal for breakfast once winter starts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the warming word after the winter letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Wheat is a grain crop, one of the principal cereals grown worldwide.

clue.text: Shine using advanced magic

parts.note: to shine at something is to excel
money advanced to someone is lent

explanation.surface: A conjuror performing brilliantly with skilled magic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Magic' is the definition, used in its informal British sense of wonderful, not sorcery.
explanation.definitionFit: In casual British speech 'magic!' means superb or wonderful, the same praise as excellent.

clue.text: This may prove a comfort to one who's about to retire

definitions.text: This may prove a comfort to one who's about to retire

parts.note: surface reading: someone nearing the end of a working career
setter's reading: to retire is also to go to bed, where a warming bedspread is welcome

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like advice on pensions and retirement gifts; 'retire' really means going to bed for the night.
explanation.definitionFit: An electrically heated bed covering warms the sheets for someone settling down to sleep.

clue.text: Get to know when definite

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
something definite is certain

explanation.surface: You only really know something once it is settled.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascertain is to find out for sure, to come to know a fact.

clue.text: Count's child on a roll at the end

parts.note: a tot is a small child
taken as written

indicators.note: only the closing letter of the word before is wanted

parts.note: the final letter of roll

explanation.surface: A nobleman's child enjoying a winning streak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Count' looks like a nobleman whose child is lucky; it is the verb meaning add up.
explanation.definitionFit: To total figures is to count them up to a sum.

clue.text: Greek hero getting cold in swirling sea?

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other
water swirling is churned round, so the letters of the word it describes are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
a chill is a cold

explanation.surface: A Greek warrior catching a chill in rough seas.
explanation.definitionFit: Achilles is the great warrior of the Trojan War in Homer's Iliad, a Greek hero.

clue.text: Drink and make merry in saloon by river

parts.note: a saloon is a type of car (a sedan)
the Ouse is an English river

explanation.surface: Drinking and partying in a saloon bar by a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saloon' suggests a bar, fitting the drinking; here it is the British word for a sedan car. 'By' places the river after it.
explanation.definitionFit: To carouse is to drink heavily and celebrate noisily with others.

clue.text: Boasted having pretty short hairstyle

indicators.note: short means cut off before its end, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: crew is an old past tense of crow, to boast
pretty means cute

explanation.surface: Someone bragging about their neat, cropped haircut.
explanation.definitionFit: A crew cut is a very short, bristly men's haircut once favoured by college rowers.

clue.text: Examine source of problem in fashionable school

parts.note: what is in is fashionable

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: a school of thought is a sect

indicators.note: the source of something is where it starts, so the first letter is taken

parts.note: the first letter of problem

explanation.surface: Looking into what's going wrong at a trendy school.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspect is to look over carefully, the same as examining something.

clue.text: Simple misprint

definitions.meaning: first meaning: plain and taken at face value
second meaning: printers' British term for a typographical error

explanation.walkthrough: In British publishing a 'literal' is a typo, a usage many solvers outside the trade won't know.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an adjective for plain, unembellished meaning and a printers' noun for a typing error.

clue.text: Confined nearby

definitions.meaning: first meaning: restricted to one part
second meaning: belonging to the neighbourhood close at hand

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective covers both something limited to a particular area and something situated in the vicinity.

clue.text: Cross, went off to expose platform

indicators.note: something gone off has gone wrong, so the letters before it are spoilt and rearranged

parts.note: all nine letters of these two words are the fodder

explanation.surface: An angry person storming off to reveal something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like the mood of someone who went off; both words are simply letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A crow's nest is a lookout platform high on a ship's mast.

clue.text: Things associated with the US male, girl put in an article

indicators.note: pieces put in another word are placed inside it

parts.note: taken as written, split to hold the others
M is the abbreviation for male
a girl's name
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A list of things linked to an American man and a girl in a newspaper article.
explanation.walkthrough: 'An article' reads as one phrase, but 'an' is the container and 'article' a separate final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Americana are artefacts and memorabilia characteristic of the culture and history of the United States.

clue.text: The radio broadcast about head of Persian goddess

indicators.note: about means going around, so the jumbled letters surround the next piece
seed broadcast is scattered widely, so the letters before it are dispersed and rearranged

parts.note: all eight letters of these two words are the fodder

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of Persian

explanation.surface: A radio programme about a Persian goddess.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphrodite is the Greek goddess of love and beauty.

clue.text: Dissenter in a Post Office, say

parts.note: taken as written
the standard abbreviation for Post Office
to say something is to state it

explanation.surface: A protester inside a post office having their say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' looks like it introduces an example; it is the verb meaning state.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostate abandons a faith or cause they once held, a dissenter from it.

clue.text: Headgear for the incompetent?

parts.note: surface reading: a cap that marks out a hopeless worker, like a dunce's cap
setter's reading: an idle or useless person is called a slouch, as in 'no slouch', so this is a hat for a slouch

explanation.walkthrough: A slouch is a lazy, inept person, so a hat 'for' one is a pun on the soft broad-brimmed hat worn by Australian soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: This soft felt hat has one brim turned down and the other pinned up, as worn by Australian troops.

clue.text: Bishop in board game in house

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
taken as written
Go is the Japanese board game of black and white stones

explanation.surface: A chess bishop on a games board at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In house' sounds like a place; 'house' alone is the definition, an old name for the numbers game.
explanation.definitionFit: Bingo was long called house or housey-housey, from the winning call of 'House!'.

clue.text: Code of honour of US president I see to

parts.note: either of the two Presidents Bush
taken as written
to see to a task is to do it

explanation.surface: A US president vowing personally to uphold a code of honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Bushido is the samurai's code of honour in feudal Japan, stressing loyalty and courage.

clue.text: Note in sombre vein

indicators.note: the answer is sitting inside the run of letters that follows

parts.note: found running across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A musical note struck in a melancholy mood.
explanation.definitionFit: A breve is a long musical note, equal to two semibreves.

clue.text: Carry mine in animal enclosure

parts.note: to carry is to bear
a coal mine is a pit

explanation.surface: Carrying something into a mine shaft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mine' looks like a possessive; it is the noun for a colliery.
explanation.definitionFit: A bear pit is a sunken enclosure where bears were kept or baited.

clue.text: Stick label back on

indicators.note: going back means the word before is read from right to left

parts.note: a tab is a small label
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to glue a label back onto something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stick' looks like the verb for gluing; it is the noun for a rod.
explanation.definitionFit: A baton is a short stick, such as a conductor's or the one passed in a relay.

clue.text: Picture, recently stolen, thrown into Italian river

indicators.note: something thrown into a river ends up inside it

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river
stolen goods still easy to trace are hot

explanation.surface: A stolen painting dumped in an Italian river.
explanation.definitionFit: A photo is a picture taken with a camera.

clue.text: Retired professors in Cambridge ultimately deserve one

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word before

parts.note: the last letter of Cambridge
to deserve something is to merit it
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Retired dons in Cambridge each finally get what they deserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Emeriti is the plural of emeritus, a professor who has retired but keeps an honorary title.

clue.text: Kill escort

definitions.meaning: first meaning: slang for eliminating someone
second meaning: to accompany someone on a date or outing

explanation.walkthrough: The pairing suggests a hitman's assignment, but the two words are independent senses of one phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to murder a target and to take someone out for an evening.

clue.text: Our excitement misplaced with canon finally giving sacrament

indicators.note: letters that are misplaced are out of position and need putting into a new order

parts.note: all thirteen letters of these two words go into the mix

indicators.note: finally picks out the last letter of the word before it

parts.note: the last letter of canon

explanation.surface: A churchman's excitement going astray at a sacred rite.
explanation.definitionFit: Extreme unction is the former Catholic name for the anointing of the sick, a sacrament given to the dying.
